data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: Information Technology Program and Project Manager Certification Requirements
extract_result.opi: Office of the Chief Information Officer – Information Resource Management

table_of_contents.section_title: IT P/PMs Certification Levels, Training Requirements, and Thresholds

actors.name: USDA Associate CIO for Information Resource Management (IRM)
USDA Agency and Staff Office CIOs

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) implements policy requirements of the Federal Acquisition Certification for Program and Project Managers (FAC-P/PM) as defined in the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP) Memorandum, Revisions to the Federal Acquisition Certification for Program and Project Managers (FAC-P/PM) dated December 16, 2013, which became effective on March 31, 2014.
cross_references: Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP) Memorandum, Revisions to the Federal Acquisition Certification for Program and Project Managers (FAC-P/PM) dated December 16, 2013

policy_statements.source_text: This DR establishes United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy, standards, certification requirements, roles and responsibilities, and authorities for the USDA information technology (IT) program and project managers (P/PMs) of USDA’s major and non-major IT investments.

This DR establishes policy that incorporates those management oversight controls and processes that are consistent with the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), P.L. 113-291, Title VIII, Subtitle D, Sections 831-837.
cross_references: Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), P.L. 113-291, Title VIII, Subtitle D, Sections 831-837

policy_statements.source_text: USDA IT P/PMs are accountable for the planning, programming, budgeting, and acquisition of USDA major IT investments, as defined in DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology Investments, and non-major IT investments that compose the USDA IT portfolio.
policy_statements.target: planning, programming, budgeting, and acquisition of USDA major IT investments
cross_references: DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology Investments

policy_statements.source_text: Skilled IT P/PMs, as part of the USDA acquisition workforce, are critical in developing accurate Government requirements, defining measurable performance metrics, and managing acquisition activities to ensure that intended USDA business and technical outcomes are achieved.
To that end, FAC-P/PM certification provides a structured approach to developing the career of USDA IT P/PMs.

The Services Acquisition Reform Act (SARA) of 2003 (41 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 1903) expanded the definition of acquisition to include key functions performed by both P/PMs, including requirements development, performance management, and technical direction.
cross_references: Services Acquisition Reform Act (SARA) of 2003 (41 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 1903)

policy_statements.source_text: OFPP Policy Letter 05-01, Developing and Managing the Acquisition Workforce, provided a broader definition of acquisition workforce and required the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) to make recommendations for a P/PM certification program.
cross_references: OFPP Policy Letter 05-01, Developing and Managing the Acquisition Workforce

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of Management and Budget’s (OMB) Capital Programming Guide, Version 3.0, emphasizes how Federal agencies have improved the way IT portfolios are managed, and have capitalized on opportunities to leverage both IT and non-IT assets across the Government, when managed by well trained and certified P/PMs.
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget’s (OMB) Capital Programming Guide, Version 3.0

policy_statements.source_text: In issuing IT-specific program and project management qualification guidance for P/PMs, OMB Memorandum 04-19, Information Technology (IT) Project Manager (PM) Qualification Guidance, states: “Qualified federal IT Project Managers are our first line of defense against the cost overruns, schedule slips and poor performance that threaten agencies’ ability to deliver efficient and effective services to citizens.”
cross_references: OMB Memorandum 04-19, Information Technology (IT) Project Manager (PM) Qualification Guidance

policy_statements.source_text: The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 U.S.C. 1401 et seq., requires Federal agencies to assess “the requirements established for agency personnel regarding knowledge and skill in information resources management and the adequacy of those requirements for facilitating the achievement of the performance goals established for information resource management.”
cross_references: Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 U.S.C. 1401 et seq.

policy_statements.source_text: In June 2015, OMB issued guidance to implement FITARA requirements.
cross_references: FITARA

policy_statements.source_text: OMB Memorandum M-15-14, Management and Oversight of Federal Information Technology, takes Clinger-Cohen a step further and instructs Federal agencies “to develop a set of competency requirements for IT staff including IT leadership positions and develop and maintain a workforce planning process to ensure the department/agency can (a) anticipate and respond to changing mission requirements, (b) maintain workforce skills in a rapidly developing IT environment, and (c) recruit and retain the IT talent needed to accomplish the mission.”
cross_references: OMB Memorandum M-15-14, Management and Oversight of Federal Information Technology
Clinger-Cohen

policy_statements.source_text: None.
This DR applies to all USDA agencies and staff offices conducting business for or on behalf of the USDA when using USDA IT resources.
policy_statements.target: all USDA agencies and staff offices
conditions: conducting business for or on behalf of the USDA
when using USDA IT resources

policy_statements.source_text: This DR sets forth a structured competency development model for all USDA IT P/PMs included in the USDA’s IT acquisition workforce serving as P/PMs.
policy_statements.target: all USDA IT P/PMs included in the USDA’s IT acquisition workforce serving as P/PMs

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA agencies and staff offices that manage major IT investments as defined in DR 3130-008; non-major IT investments as presented in the USDA Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control Guide; and investments owned or operated by USDA.
policy_statements.target: all USDA agencies and staff offices
conditions: that manage major IT investments as defined in DR 3130-008; non-major IT investments as presented in the USDA Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control Guide; and investments owned or operated by USDA
cross_references: USDA Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control Guide

policy_statements.source_text: This DR covers all IT investments under development, modernization, and enhancement (DME) and those in operations and maintenance (O&M) that are reported by the USDA in the annual OMB A-11 budget submission.
policy_statements.target: all IT investments under development, modernization, and enhancement (DME) and those in operations and maintenance (O&M)
conditions: that are reported by the USDA in the annual OMB A-11 budget submission
cross_references: OMB A-11

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to the above-listed investments throughout their entire life cycle, regardless of funding source.
conditions: throughout their entire life cycle, regardless of funding source

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to USDA IT P/PMs that are involved in the acquisition or management of USDA major and non-major IT investments where they have:
conditions: that are involved in the acquisition or management of USDA major and non-major IT investments

policy_statements.source_text: Direct program or project management responsibility in one or more phases of the USDA life cycle (i.e., initiation, investment, requirements analysis, design, development and test, implementation, and operations, maintenance, and disposition);
Authority and responsibility for overseeing multiple phases of the acquisition investment process; and
Responsibility for leading or participating on a cross-agency or acquisition investment program for a major portion or all of the investment lifecycle.
USDA IT P/PMs assigned to USDA major IT investments must also meet the requirements of the Federal IT Project Manager Guidance Matrix; and
policy_statements.target: requirements of the Federal IT Project Manager Guidance Matrix
conditions: assigned to USDA major IT investments
cross_references: Federal IT Project Manager Guidance Matrix

policy_statements.source_text: USDA IT P/PMs certified under the FAC-P/PM program are considered to have the general competencies and experience needed for identifying qualified IT P/PMs.
policy_statements.resulting_status: general competencies and experience needed for identifying qualified IT P/PMs
conditions: certified under the FAC-P/PM program

policy_statements.source_text: Private industry or contractors are not eligible for FAC-P/PM certification.
Agencies and staff offices shall comply with the guidance contained in this DR.
An agency and staff office will be allowed to develop specific policy for their IT P/PMs, but that policy may not be less restrictive or less comprehensive as defined in this DR.
policy_statements.target: specific policy for their IT P/PMs

policy_statements.source_text: This DR shall be incorporated by reference into applicable contract language or memoranda of agreement under separate cover, as appropriate.
conditions: as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: All IT P/PMs assigned to acquisitions of major IT investments must be senior-level certified as described in the FAC-P/PM revision memo and as determined by the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) and the Chief Acquisition Officer (CAO).
conditions: assigned to acquisitions of major IT investments
cross_references: FAC-P/PM revision memo

policy_statements.source_text: All IT P/PMs assigned to acquisitions of non-major IT investments must be mid-level certified as determined by the USDA CIO and the CAO.
conditions: assigned to acquisitions of non-major IT investments

policy_statements.source_text: In the event that all FAC P/PM senior level certification requirements have not been completed prior to selection or assignment to a major IT investment or acquisition, the IT P/PM has 12 months from the date of assignment to complete all certification requirements.
conditions: In the event that all FAC P/PM senior level certification requirements have not been completed prior to selection or assignment to a major IT investment or acquisition

policy_statements.source_text: Certification Waivers, Extensions, and Compliance
Certification requirements may not be waived; however, the timeframe to meet certification requirements may be extended on a case-by-case basis by the USDA CIO and the CAO;
conditions: on a case-by-case basis

policy_statements.source_text: USDA FAC-P/PM certification is valid Departmentwide for employees transferring to another USDA agency or staff office;
conditions: for employees transferring to another USDA agency or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO and CAO will review all written extension requests and determine whether granting the extension is in the best interest of the USDA; and
Failure to attain within the 12 month period the required certification shall be grounds for removal as an IT P/PM for major and non-major IT investments.
policy_statements.target: removal as an IT P/PM for major and non-major IT investments
conditions: Failure to attain within the 12 month period the required certification

policy_statements.source_text: Cross-Agency Applicability
FAC-P/PM certification is transferable to other Federal civilian agencies.
USDA shall accept FAC-P/PM certifications from other civilian agencies as evidence that an IT P/PM meets and has maintained the core project management training and experience;
policy_statements.target: FAC-P/PM certifications from other civilian agencies

policy_statements.source_text: In order to be accepted, a transferring employee’s active certification must be documented and accurately recorded in the FAI Training Application System (FAITAS);
conditions: In order to be accepted

policy_statements.source_text: USDA shall adhere to FAI guidelines to determine if non-Federal Government credentials will be eligible for full or partial consideration under this DR.
Additional training may be required for issuance of USDA-specific FAC-P/PM certification;
conditions: for issuance of USDA-specific FAC-P/PM certification

policy_statements.source_text: See Appendix B for the USDA P/PM certification levels, requisite training requirements, and IT investment funding thresholds; and
See Appendix C for a sample USDA IT P/PM resume template that illustrates needed input for FAC-P/PM certification review and determination.
This resume template can be used as a handy reference tool by IT P/PMs to keep a record of their relevant certification courses and experience.
The USDA CIO shall:
Be responsible for IT-related FAC-P/PM program administration through the issuance of policy and guidance in concert with the CAO;
Have an active role in defining an USDA-wide process to advise on planning program management as presented in FITARA requirements C1 and C2;
cross_references: FITARA
policy_statements.target: USDA-wide process to advise on planning program management

policy_statements.source_text: Review and render decisions on waivers and extensions in concert with the CAO;
Shall review and remove IT P/PMs that fail to attain a required certification in coordination with the CAO;
conditions: that fail to attain a required certification

policy_statements.source_text: Be responsible for the periodic review of agencies and staff offices’ IT-specific FAC-P/PM certifications and maintenance records to ensure compliance with USDA and Federal policies and guidance; and
policy_statements.target: agencies and staff offices’ IT-specific FAC-P/PM certifications and maintenance records

policy_statements.source_text: Shall regularly assess USDA IT P/PMs using competencies from the FAC P/PM competency model and other USDA-related IT competencies; determine competency strengths and weaknesses among FAC P/PMs; and develop strategies, including Departmentwide FAC P/PM training programs to close gaps.
The USDA CAO shall:
Be responsible for the FAC-P/PM program administration through the issuance of policy and guidance for acquisitions;
Appoint the USDA Acquisition Career Manager (ACM);
Be responsible for the periodic review of agency and staff office FAC-P/PM certifications and maintenance records;
policy_statements.target: agency and staff office FAC-P/PM certifications and maintenance records

policy_statements.source_text: May review and remove FAC-P/PMs that fail to attain a required certification;
conditions: that fail to attain a required certification

policy_statements.source_text: Establish FAC-P/PM training requirements; and
Develop and maintain an acquisition management career program to ensure USDA has a competent, professional workforce to accomplish its mission.
The USDA ACM shall:
Manage the P/PMs acquisition workforce, including identifying training requirements and other workforce development strategies;
Administer the Department’s FAC-P/PM certification program;
Develop and maintain Departmental policies and procedures for workforce management consistent with those established by OFPP, as appropriate;
policy_statements.target: Departmental policies and procedures for workforce management
conditions: consistent with those established by OFPP, as appropriate

policy_statements.source_text: Recommend extensions to the FAC-P/PM requirements to the CAO, as needed, and in accordance with the qualification standards; and
conditions: as needed
in accordance with the qualification standards

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that continuous learning requirements are monitored.
The USDA Associate CIO for Information Resource Management (IRM) shall:
Support and monitor the IT P/PMs certification process, policy, and guidance;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Associate CIO for Information Resource Management (IRM)
policy_statements.target: IT P/PMs certification process, policy, and guidance

policy_statements.source_text: Appoint an IT ACM Designee; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Associate CIO for Information Resource Management (IRM)

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure compliance with provisions contained in this DR.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Associate CIO for Information Resource Management (IRM)

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA IT ACM Designee shall:
Assist all USDA IT P/PMs in reviewing their qualifications against requisite P/PM certification levels and training requirements provided in this DR;
Assist all USDA IT P/PMs in submitting appropriate documentation for determining proper FAC-P/PM certification level.
USDA Agency and Staff Office CIOs shall:
Ensure that P/PMs are FAC-P/PM certified at the appropriate level for major and non-major IT investments; and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Agency and Staff Office CIOs

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that training information for P/PMs is validated via supporting documentation, in accordance with this DR, and is maintained in FAITAS.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Agency and Staff Office CIOs

policy_statements.source_text: USDA IT P/PMs shall:
Possess and maintain the requisite FAC-P/PM certification level required to manage a major or non-major USDA IT investment;

Participate in regular assessments to determine individual competency strengths and weaknesses; identify strategies to strengthen their weaknesses; and if applicable, populate their individual development plans (IDP) with identified competencies and developmental needs to facilitate discussion with supervisors to ensure developmental needs are met per DR 4040-410, Creating Individual Development Plans (IDP);
cross_references: DR 4040-410, Creating Individual Development Plans (IDP)

policy_statements.source_text: Submit the appropriate documentation for certification and maintenance, to include updates and annual reporting of training, professional activities, education and experience that are used to meet Continuous Learning Points (CLP) in FAITAS.
policy_statements.target: appropriate documentation for certification and maintenance

extract_result.purpose:
a. This Departmental Regulation (DR) implements policy requirements of the Federal Acquisition Certification for Program and Project Managers (FAC-P/PM) as defined in the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP) Memorandum, Revisions to the Federal Acquisition Certification for Program and Project Managers (FAC-P/PM) dated December 16, 2013, which became effective on March 31, 2014.
b. This DR establishes United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy, standards, certification requirements, roles and responsibilities, and authorities for the USDA information technology (IT) program and project managers (P/PMs) of USDA’s major and non-major IT investments.
c. This DR establishes policy that incorporates those management oversight controls and processes that are consistent with the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), P.L. 113-291, Title VIII, Subtitle D, Sections 831-837.
extract_result.scope:
a. This DR applies to all USDA agencies and staff offices conducting business for or on behalf of the USDA when using USDA IT resources.
b. This DR sets forth a structured competency development model for all USDA IT P/PMs included in the USDA’s IT acquisition workforce serving as P/PMs.
c. This DR applies to all USDA agencies and staff offices that manage major IT investments as defined in DR 3130-008; non-major IT investments as presented in the USDA Information Technology Capital Planning and Investment Control Guide; and investments owned or operated by USDA.
d. This DR covers all IT investments under development, modernization, and enhancement (DME) and those in operations and maintenance (O&M) that are reported by the USDA in the annual OMB A-11 budget submission.
e. This DR applies to the above-listed investments throughout their entire life cycle, regardless of funding source.
f. This DR applies to USDA IT P/PMs that are involved in the acquisition or management of USDA major and non-major IT investments where they have:
(1) Direct program or project management responsibility in one or more phases of the USDA life cycle (i.e., initiation, investment, requirements analysis, design, development and test, implementation, and operations, maintenance, and disposition);
(2) Authority and responsibility for overseeing multiple phases of the acquisition investment process; and
(3) Responsibility for leading or participating on a cross-agency or acquisition investment program for a major portion or all of the investment lifecycle.
g. USDA IT P/PMs assigned to USDA major IT investments must also meet the requirements of the Federal IT Project Manager Guidance Matrix; and
h. USDA IT P/PMs certified under the FAC-P/PM program are considered to have the general competencies and experience needed for identifying qualified IT P/PMs. Private industry or contractors are not eligible for FAC-P/PM certification.

a. This Departmental Regulation (DR) implements policy requirements of the Federal Acquisition Certification for Program and Project Managers (FAC-P/PM) as defined in the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP) Memorandum,  *Revisions to the Federal Acquisition Certification for Program and Project Managers (FAC-P/PM)*  dated December 16, 2013, which became effective on March 31, 2014.

This DR establishes United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy, standards, certification requirements, roles and responsibilities, and authorities for the USDA information technology (IT) program and project managers (P/PMs) of USDA’s major and non-major IT investments.

c. This DR establishes policy that incorporates those management oversight controls and processes that are consistent with the *Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act* ( FITARA ), P.L. 113-291, Title VIII, Subtitle D, Sections 831-837.

USDA IT P/PMs are accountable for the planning, programming, budgeting, and acquisition of USDA major IT investments, as defined in  DR 3130-008 , *Definition of Major Information Technology Investments*, and non-major IT investments that compose the USDA IT portfolio

Skilled IT P/PMs, as part of the USDA acquisition workforce, are critical in developing accurate Government requirements, defining measurable performance metrics, and managing acquisition activities to ensure that intended USDA business and technical outcomes are achieved.
To that end, FAC-P/PM certification provides a structured approach to developing the career of USDA IT P/PMs.

The *Services Acquisition Reform Act* ( SARA ) of 2003 (41 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 1903) expanded the definition of acquisition to include key functions performed by both P/PMs, including requirements development, performance management, and technical direction.  OFPP Policy Letter 05-01 , *Developing and Managing the Acquisition Workforce*, provided a broader definition of acquisition workforce and required the Federal Acquisition Institute (FAI) to make recommendations for a P/PM certification program.

The Office of Management and Budget’s (OMB)  *Capital Programming Guide, Version 3.0* , emphasizes how Federal agencies have improved the way IT portfolios are managed, and have capitalized on opportunities to leverage both IT and non-IT assets across the Government, when managed by well trained and certified P/PMs.

In issuing IT-specific program and project management qualification guidance for P/PMs, OMB  Memorandum 04-19 , *Information Technology (IT) Project Manager (PM) Qualification Guidance*, states: “Qualified federal IT Project Managers are our first line of defense against the cost overruns, schedule slips and poor performance that threaten agencies’ ability to deliver efficient and effective services to citizens.”
